resources.string: Keeps Capri running and holds her menu.
On your screen. Tap here for my menu.
Capri lives on top of your apps and tells you what Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity is doing (in Termux on this phone, or on your PC through Wi-Fi).
Command copied. Paste it in Termux and press Enter.
She is on your screen. Long-press her for her menu.
Grant the two permissions, then start her.
Nothing yet. If she does not show up, what went wrong appears here.
Opens her panel over your screen: free with no account, a key (Groq, Gemini and NVIDIA are free), or your PC\'s Ollama over Wi-Fi. No terminal.
See your notifications and music (optional): she jumps on them
Confirm it on the screen Android shows
Allow Capri to install apps, then come back and tap Update.
The update didn\'t work from here: its page opens so you can download it.
This version was signed differently: uninstall Capri once and install it again. After that, updates install over.
Tap to update, no need to uninstall.
Hey, choom. I’m Capri. I’ll live on top of your apps, chat with you and tell you what your AI is up to. First, four quick things.
Your name or a nickname. I’ll use it now and then. You can change it later in Settings.
To talk with you I need an AI, %1$s.
Pick one. You can change it any time in Settings.
One tap and done. Goes through the internet (Pollinations).
Groq, Gemini and NVIDIA are free: open their page, make a key, copy it and paste it here.
Your PC is her brain over Wi-Fi. In Ollama turn on “Expose Ollama to the network” and type the PC’s IP here.
That key doesn’t work. Check you copied all of it.
No answer (%1$s). Check the address or your connection.
Now the permissions. I’ll tell you what each one is for.
The needed ones come first. You can give the optional ones any time from the Permissions tab.
It’s how I exist on your phone: without it I can’t show up over anything. Your taps still reach your apps; only I and my panels can be touched.
Android needs a pinned notification so it doesn’t close me. It’s also my panel: Menu, Put away and Quit, and my winks.

So I can sit on your music with its controls and jump on your notices. I only see the app and the title, never the message, and nothing leaves the phone. Heads-up: with this on, some banking apps block you; if you use one, better leave it off.
So I can update myself from GitHub without uninstalling. Android still asks you to confirm each time.
All set, %1$s. See you on top of your apps.
Long-press me for my menu, drag me to throw me, and pet me with two fingers.
First let her show over other apps.
What Capri can do on your phone, and why she needs it.
It downloads in your browser. When it\'s done, open it and tap Update: it installs over this one, nothing lost.

Some banking apps block you if another app shows on top or can see notifications, even if it reads nothing from them. I never read anything from your bank or send your data anywhere. If your bank complains: turn off “See your notifications” and put me away (“Put away”, in my notification) before opening it.
Developer mode: the log shows in Settings.

Only if you turn on “Talk to her” in Settings, and only with the screen on. Your phone\'s own speech recognizer turns what you say into words; I only keep what comes after my name, and I never record audio. Android shows the microphone dot while I\'m listening. Heads-up: some banking apps and antivirus apps get wary of apps with the microphone; if yours complains, turn it off.

Say “Capri” and then what you want: “Capri, what time is it?”, “Capri, open Spotify”, “Capri, next song”, “Capri, turn on the flashlight”, “Capri, set a 10 minute timer”, “Capri, hide”. Anything else goes to her AI, and she answers out loud. Only with the screen on.
On: she\'s listening for her name.
Without the microphone she can\'t hear you.
This phone has no speech recognizer (install or update the Google app).
The microphone is busy (a call or another app).
Paused while a video or music plays: listening would pause it. Back on its own when it ends.
No microphone permission: give it in Permissions.
This phone has no speech recognizer (install or update the Google app).
The speech recognizer failed (error %1$s). Trying again…
What you can ask her, out loud or typed in her chat.

string-array.item: Turn it on in Settings → Talk to her. Say “Capri” and what you want; if you only say “Capri”, she listens for a few seconds. All of this also works typed in her chat.
“Capri, play Never Fade Away on YouTube”
While something plays she doesn’t listen (it would pause it): use her music bar or type it in her chat.
“Capri, turn on the flashlight” · “turn off the flashlight”
“Capri, how much battery do I have?”
“Capri, how much free space is left?”
“Capri, open wifi settings” (or bluetooth, sound, display…)
“Capri, remind me to call mom in 1 hour”
“Capri, remind me tomorrow at 9 to take out the trash”
“Capri, gamer mode” (off in Settings or her menu)
“Capri, translate this into English” (what’s on your screen)
“Capri, give me a tip” (for the game on your screen)
“Capri, look at my screen” (Android asks you first; it needs an AI that sees pictures, like Gemini)
Live: Settings → Let her see your screen → Watch live
Anything else goes to her AI and she answers out loud: “Capri, tell me a joke”, “Capri, how do you say cat in Japanese?”

resources.string: Capri news before anyone else, ideas, bugs, and people who have her on their phone too. Come to the Discord and follow me on TikTok.

She stays exactly where you put her, even in the air: let go of her and she floats there. She doesn’t wander off or jump onto your notifications, and flinging her doesn’t throw her around, so she never gets mad about it. Put her in a corner or next to your chats and she stays.

Only her green mask stays on screen, with her eyes open, and she keeps commenting from there (your screen, your games, her chat). Drag it with a finger wherever it bothers you least; tap it for her menu. Handy if you like her big: when she’s out she’s big, as an icon she takes almost nothing.

For when you play: she sits small and half see-through in a corner to watch you play (how see-through: her Wardrobe › Effects), only her face takes touches, her cards stay away, she stops listening, and now and then she cheers you on. Also in her menu or by saying “Capri, gamer mode”. Off when you tap it again or restart her.
On its own when a game opens

It turns on when you open a game and off when you leave. It needs “Usage access” in Android’s settings (she only sees which app is open, nothing inside it). Heads up: some banking and antivirus apps distrust that permission; if yours complains, leave this off.
Find Capri in the list and turn on “Permit usage access”.
She stays on your screen but your touches go through her to your apps. Her face still takes touches: drag her by it, or hold it for her menu.

“Capri, look at my screen” (or the button) lets her look once and comment. Live, she looks now and then and when you switch apps, until you turn it off. Android asks you each time it starts and shows its recording notice while she can see. The picture only goes to her chat\'s AI; banking apps come out black. It needs an AI that sees pictures, like Gemini (its key is free): Capri\'s free AI can\'t see.

After a chat, Capri notes down what matters (what you like, the people you talk about, what’s going on with you) so she remembers it next time. It stays only on this phone; to note it down she asks her AI once per chat.
She doesn’t remember anything yet. Chat with her for a while.
Leave it empty to keep the key you already saved
This only replays her welcome. Your AI, your key and her settings stay as they are; on the AI step, just tap Next.
She tells you when your phone is charged to the percent you choose, and when it’s running low. Android tells her the battery; no permission needed.
Tell me when it charges to
Tell me when it drops to
After this long on your phone without putting it down, she tells you to rest your eyes. Turning the screen off five minutes counts as a break.

👁 = can look at your screen. They can: Gemini, OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral and NVIDIA (she picks one of their models that sees). They can’t: DeepSeek and the free AI. With Ollama, only vision models (llava, gemma3, qwen-vl).

With people or a TV around, she can think she heard her name. Stricter: she only answers when “Capri” is the first thing you say, and said clearly. Stricter also ignores what she hears while the phone is moving in your hand.

Everyday outfits and Cyberpunk: Edgerunners ones (David, Lucy, Rebecca, Kiwi, Talia…), accessories, auras and the Sandevistan, and how see-through she is. While you dress her she climbs on top of the panel, so you see every change on her.
And now she moves frame by frame, like in the anime: she dances, sleeps curled up, watches you play, listens to your music with you, gets dizzy if you throw her…
Open it any time: hold her and tap “Dress her”, or say “Capri, get dressed”.

How she sounds in this language, as people talk in each place (it also helps her understand you). If your phone has no voice for one, she uses its usual one for the language; Google’s voice engine has most of them.

In gamer mode, with her live look on (she’s watching your screen), every few minutes she gives you a tip for the game you’re playing. You can also ask her any time: “Capri, give me a tip”, “what do I do here?”. Her AI has to see pictures.

For when you’re live (TikTok, Twitch, YouTube, Kick…): she reads your viewers’ comments off your screen and answers them out loud, as your co-host. No login and no connection to those apps: she only sees your screen (Android asks you to share it). Her AI has to see pictures. Also “Capri, streaming mode”. Off when you tap it again or restart her.
Heard “%1$s” while the phone was moving: ignored (its rustle, not you).

Light mode draws her with fewer pixels and leaves out the blur behind her menus: she runs smoother on older phones and uses less battery. Automatic turns it on for phones with little memory or an old Android.

Capri is drawn by Android System WebView, and the one on this phone (version %1$d) is too old for her: she may not show up or may freeze. Update it from the Play Store (it’s free and safe, it’s part of Android) and start her again.
Heard something far away (the TV, someone else): ignored it.
What Capri knows about you: what she calls you, your birthday, what she remembers and how she looks after you.
How your Capri looks, behaves and sounds.
What’s general: her permissions, the language, her AI, her ears, her modes and how the app runs.
On that day she celebrates you: confetti, she wishes you a happy birthday out loud and throws her party. She can also ask you about it in her chat.

Once a day the app sends a random number made up the first time (not your phone’s or your account’s), the app’s version, its language and the Android version, so Emma knows how many people use Capri. Nothing else: no name, no chats, nothing from your phone.
With ghost mode on, your touches also go through her notification and music cards. Off: only she lets them through, and her cards can still be touched.

When you pull down your notification panel or quick settings, Capri peeks in from the side and waves. Android only lets an app above that panel through Accessibility, so it’s turned on there: Accessibility › Capri. She reads nothing there and touches nothing: she’s only told that the panel opened. Some banking apps refuse to open while any app has Accessibility on. If Android says it’s a restricted setting: App info › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings.

Capri peeks into your notification panel and quick settings when you pull them down. This only tells the app that Android’s panel opened: it doesn’t read what’s on your screen, doesn’t touch anything and doesn’t watch other apps.
Capri peeks in when you pull down the notification panel
Capri’s quick things: start her, talk, look at your screen, dress her
Tell me which days you have class and at what time: an hour before, my special notification reaches you. It all stays on your phone.
If you want, I read your calendar to remind you of what’s coming: the evening before and an hour before. I only read it, I never change anything, and nothing leaves your phone.
Without the calendar permission I can’t see it. You can grant it in Android’s settings.
Capri reminds you of your classes and what’s coming in your calendar.
%1$s at %2$s. Grab your stuff, eat something and don’t be late. I’ll save you a seat.
At %1$s. I’ll remember it for you, but you too, okay?
It’s all day. Get ready from today.
Today’s the day, choom. Make it count.
Almost time, choom. I’m telling you early so you don’t have to run.
Tell us what happened and it reaches Emma on Discord. Along with it go the app’s version, your Android and phone model, and Capri’s internal error log, without your name, your messages or your keys.
What happened? What were you doing?
Tell us a bit more about what happened.
Sent. Thank you, choom: Emma will look at it.
You’ve sent several already. Try again in an hour.
Reports aren’t being received right now. Try again later.
No connection. Check your internet and try again.
It couldn’t be sent. Try again later.
Reads visible text or clicks one visible item only when explicitly requested.
Optional. Does not continuously collect screen contents.
